Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada has insisted that some of the criticism directed at the club’s hierarchy has gone too far, although he admits that supporters have every reason to be frustrated with the team’s performances. Speaking in a rare interview with Sky Sports on Friday, Berrada acknowledged the anger among United supporters over the club’s disappointing position in the Premier League but maintained that criticism of the leadership should remain within reasonable limits. “Being in this position comes naturally with the criticism and scrutiny we’re going to get. We accept it. Some of it is fair, some of it does cross the line,” he said. Berrada also pointed to social media as a major contributor to the negative atmosphere surrounding the club, arguing that some individuals deliberately generate damaging stories to attract engagement and attention. United’s director of football, Jason Wilcox, has come under particular pressure from supporters following questions over the club’s summer recruitment. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. NFL legend Tom Brady in talks to buy Chelsea stake – Report EPL: Caicedo, Martinez fit for Chelsea’s Leeds clash EPL: Prove loyalty to Tottenham fans, De Zerbi tells Mudryk However, Berrada has defended the club’s transfer business, insisting that the additions of Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, alongside Marcus Rashford’s return from his loan spell at Barcelona, have improved the squad. He admitted that United could have signed another defender but explained that the club was unwilling to spend heavily on players they were not convinced would improve the team. Meanwhile, new head coach Mauricio Pochettino has expressed his desire to have greater involvement in the club’s football decisions, particularly future squad planning and recruitment. Pochettino confirmed that he would take responsibility for selecting the starting XI and making substitutions but added that he wanted to be involved in the major decisions concerning the squad. The comments highlight the challenges facing United’s leadership as the club attempts to rebuild its fortunes while dealing with growing pressure from supporters.
